product.id: H. H. Windsor, Mission Furniture, Part Three (1912)
product.name: Piano bench
product.introText: A piano bench with slatted ends from "Mission Furniture: How to Make It, Part Three" by H. H. Windsor (Popular Mechanics Company, Chicago, 1912; public domain in the USA, Project Gutenberg ebook 23666). The book comes with no 3D parts: all 18 pieces are modelled from its stock list and its one dimensioned drawing, inches converted to millimetres, and shown already cut. The sizes of the tenons and the depth of the housed ends are not in the book and are assumed.
product.partsSummary: Stock list from the book: 1 top, 1 by 16-1/2 by 40-1/2 in.  4 posts, 1-1/2 by 1-1/2 by 20 in.  2 rails, 7/8 by 4-1/4 by 36 in.  2 rails, 7/8 by 4-1/4 by 13 in.  2 lower rails, 7/8 by 2-1/2 by 13 in.  1 stretcher, 7/8 by 3-3/4 by 36 in.  6 slats, 3/8 by 1-1/4 by 11 in.  Not shown: hot glue; blocks and screws or angle irons for the top.

steps.title: Put the ends of the bench together
steps.text: Assemble the parts, using good hot glue. Put the ends of the bench together first. [Each end: the slats, housed with their whole end, into the lower rail; the upper rail onto the slats; a post onto each pair of tenons. The glue is not shown.]

moves.label: rails and slats of the second end into a post

steps.title: Place the stretcher and side rails
steps.text: When the glue has hardened on these, place the stretcher and side rails.

steps.title: Fasten the top to the frame
steps.text: Fasten the top to the frame from the under side, either by glued blocks and screws or by angle irons. [The blocks, screws and angle irons are not in the stock list and are not shown.]
